notes: The exact deployed build identities the live canary requires. `ghl-pilot preflight` compares this against what the health endpoints actually report and refuses live mode unless every checkpoint matches exactly.

`required_commit` is the reviewed revision that must be built and activated. A revision being merged and reviewed is not activation; only a health endpoint reporting that commit, clean and activated, satisfies a checkpoint.
ACT-REV-01 and ACT-REV-02 are the historical bootstrap and review-repair checkpoints. Their receipts must already be recorded; ACT-REV-03 and ACT-REV-04 supersede them.
A satisfied preflight is a precondition for the canary, never an authorization for it. Activation and the canary each require Joel's separate approval.

checkpoints.title: Manager build carrying the bounded mission policies and the lifecycle request surface
checkpoints.rollback: Re-activate the previously running Manager build and confirm its health endpoint reports the prior commit, clean and activated. The lifecycle request surface is additive, so a rollback leaves the operator start_agent_mission path intact; no mission state migration is required.
smoke_checks: preflight_agent_mission returns allowed for each of the three target project IDs and refused for a wrong-scope pair, with the registry and policy hashes matching the reviewed build.
request_agent_mission refuses shared-manager with the phase-0 message while the operator start path still succeeds.
check_agent_mission from a foreign connector scope is indistinguishable from an unknown mission id.
checkpoints.note: Production ran a pre-GHL-005 build when this spec was written; the request surface it must carry is absent there.

checkpoints.title: Contribution coordinator and review build carrying the claim reducer, conductor, and scope routing
checkpoints.rollback: Re-activate the last known-good coordinator build and confirm its health endpoint reports that commit, clean and activated. Before rolling back, release any open claim so no lease is held by a build that no longer runs; claim and attention state is reconstructed from GitHub events, so no local state is lost.
smoke_checks: The claim reducer reconstructs a known issue's state from its GitHub comments and reports the expected generation and derived state.
The configured contributor identity resolves to kehle-contributor-agent and the reviewer identity is distinct from it and from the owner.
A personal-scope attention route records an owner-attention.v1 event on the pull request and makes no UCLA Project Manager call.
Write paths remain disabled until the canary step that enables them.
checkpoints.note: The deployed build was the GHL-002-only revision when this spec was written, missing GHL-004, GHL-006, and GHL-008.
